title: The re-staffed compiler seat reads the rejection reason in its mission, and a real-process journey proves reject, re-plan, approve
description:
SPIDR child 2b of task-957bccf162b446f3a4db46b56e8e8f3a (grandparent task-6061e05cd17540a1bbe08b965da65b64 - note: the parent's description carries a typo'd grandparent id; the parentTaskId FIELD is authoritative). dependsOn child 2a task-138fab3075884df98c3c220e74c1a3e9 (offers + compiler follow the current run) AND the two other rows that edit apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts (task-4109c1a0 provider pause, task-7945f38d reclaim pass) - serialised so no two rows edit the pre-existing over-cap main file at once. Filed by architect-16a01670 2026-09-04, measured at main 9e9b7b04.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: (a) the mission text a re-staffed compiler seat receives after a REJECT; (b) the real-process journey. No offer/dispatcher/read change (2a), no UI (child 3).

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- The compiler mission quotes the goal's operator instructions between `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` markers with the REPLAN sentence (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts:133-138, `compilerMission` :78); the text comes from `compilerInstructions(goalId)` in agent-wrapper-main.ts:238-250 (reads the goal catalog brief). The rejection reason lives on the REJECTED run's `approval.decide_intent` decision result (`decisionReason`, child 1 task-37801090) and the rejected run is reachable from the goal's immutable `planningRunRef` through child 1's `currentPlanningRun` fold (successorRunId on the PlanningRunRejected event). FEATURE (a): a new pure module apps/daemon/src/planning/rejection-instructions.ts (+ .js + test) exporting `latestRejectionReason(store, projectId, planningRunRef): { reason: string; rejectedRunId: string } | null` (walk the run chain from the immutable ref; the LATEST rejected run's decisionReason; null when never rejected; never throws) and `composeCompilerInstructions(brief: string | null, rejection): string | null` returning the brief plus, when a rejection exists, the sentence `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason verbatim>. Submit a DIFFERENT decomposition that addresses it.`; agent-wrapper-main.ts's `compilerInstructions` calls it (growth <= 6 lines on the over-cap file; a source-text pin in agent-wrapper-main.test.ts like the fence pin at :135-166). The marker fence: child 1 stores the reason verbatim - the composer must neutralise a reason containing the marker text (`<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` / `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>`) so a hostile reason cannot close the operator block early (replace the marker sequences, assert it).
- FEATURE (b), the journey, in the NODE e2e lane (`pnpm test:e2e` = vitest over tests/**/*.test.ts; tests/e2e/foundation holds the J-series harnesses: j4-replan-harness.ts + j4-replan-handoff.e2e.test.ts (replan through a successor goal, real daemon + real wrapper + fake-agent.mjs seat double), j1-loop-harness.ts, e2e-harness.ts, e2e-process.ts, fake-agent.mjs) - measure how J4 scripts the seat double's MCP calls and drives the wrapper, then add `tests/e2e/foundation/j5-plan-reject-replan.e2e.test.ts` (+ a j5 harness only if J4's cannot be parameterised - prefer reuse): a source-bound goal compiles (the double submits a one-node decomposition), the operator REJECTs with a reason over the real HTTP wire (approval.decide_intent, decision REJECT), the wrapper re-staffs the compiler step, the double's mission carries `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason>` (the double echoes its mission to a file the test reads), the double submits a DIFFERENT decomposition (new node key), the successor is offered for approval, the operator APPROVEs, the activation event is read back from the store. Every process real except the seat.
definitionOfDone: rejection-instructions.test.ts over a REAL store using child 1's reject fixture: never rejected -> null and the brief passes through unchanged; rejected once -> the composed text ends with `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason>. Submit a DIFFERENT decomposition that addresses it.` and names the rejected run; rejected twice -> the LATEST reason; a reason containing the marker sequences is neutralised (the composed text contains no `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` inside the sentence); a corrupt run chain -> null, never a throw.

agent-wrapper-main.ts wires the composer into `compilerInstructions` (source-text pin: the call text present exactly once, positive control that stripping it reds the pin); the compiler mission for a rejected goal, built through `compilerMission` with that instructions string, contains the sentence between the operator markers (agent-mission-text.test.ts arm or the main pin plus a compilerMission arm - name which).

Real-process journey in the node e2e lane: compile -> REJECT with reason (real HTTP approval.decide_intent) -> re-staffed seat double reads the reason in its mission (asserted from the double's echoed mission) -> submits a different decomposition -> the successor is offered for approval -> APPROVE activates it (activation event read back from the store); `pnpm test:e2e` count line quoted with this test listed; teardown proves no surviving process.

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`; rejection-instructions.ts <= 120 lines; agent-wrapper-main.ts growth <= 6 (pre-existing size recorded); sources ASCII-only; every arm mutated red once.
taskRails: VERBATIM REASON, FENCED MARKERS: the reason reaches the seat verbatim except the two marker sequences, which are neutralised - never dropped silently, never rewritten into the brief.
NO offer/dispatcher/read/UI change (2a, child 3); the only production edits are the new planning module and the six-line wiring in agent-wrapper-main.ts.
REAL PROCESSES in the journey (daemon, wrapper, store); only the seat is doubled, and it must go through the real MCP wire with a scoped bearer, never a store write.

implementationPlan.description: VERIFY THE THREE PREREQUISITES AND RE-MEASURE, NO EDITS. Confirmed by the architect at plan time; re-run them because the checkout is shared. (a) Child 1's fold landed: apps/daemon/src/planning/current-planning-run.ts exists and carries `successorRunId` (:29, read at :77-79) — this row walks the run chain through it. (b) task-4109c1a0 (provider pause) and task-7945f38d (reclaim pass) are DONE; task-138fab3075884df98c3c220e74c1a3e9 (2a, offers + compiler follow the current run) was still WORKING at plan time. All three are dependsOn precisely because they edit apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, which is 477 lines and already over the size cap — the serialisation exists so two rows never edit it at once. If 2a has not landed, report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds naming it rather than editing the file concurrently. (c) Re-measure the two seams: the operator markers at agent-mission-text.ts:138 (`<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS\n...\nOPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>`) and `compilerInstructions` at agent-wrapper-main.ts:244. RECORD agent-wrapper-main.ts's exact pre-change line count now — DoD 4 caps this row's growth at SIX lines and the number is meaningless without the baseline. (d) NOTE A CONCURRENT EDITOR: task-f79d38b119984ae1ae51eba887a28b7d is rewriting the compiler mission sentence in agent-mission-text.ts under the fence-lift ruling. This row does not edit that file's production text — it composes the INSTRUCTIONS string that flows into it — but if DoD 2 lands its arm in agent-mission-text.test.ts, expect a rebase there.

THE PURE MODULE, tests first, in a new apps/daemon/src/planning/rejection-instructions.ts (+ its `.js` bridge — a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Two exports, both PURE: `latestRejectionReason(store, projectId, planningRunRef)` walks the run chain from the goal's IMMUTABLE ref through child 1's fold and returns `{ reason, rejectedRunId }` for the LATEST rejected run, or null when never rejected — and NEVER THROWS, including on a corrupt chain; and `composeCompilerInstructions(brief, rejection)` returning the brief plus, when a rejection exists, the sentence `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason verbatim>. Submit a DIFFERENT decomposition that addresses it.` Keep it under 120 lines (DoD 4). Write the test first over a REAL store using child 1's reject fixture: never rejected -> null and the brief passes through UNCHANGED (byte-identical, not merely non-empty); rejected once -> the composed text ends with that exact sentence and names the rejected run; rejected TWICE -> the LATEST reason, which is the arm that catches a fold returning the first match; a corrupt run chain -> null, never a throw.

THE MARKER FENCE — the security-shaped correctness arm this module exists to get right (task rail 1). Child 1 stores the operator's rejection reason VERBATIM, and the compiler mission embeds the instructions between `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` and `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` (agent-mission-text.ts:138). A reason CONTAINING either marker sequence would close the operator block early and let the remainder of the reason read to the seat as mission-level text outside the quoted block. `composeCompilerInstructions` must NEUTRALISE both marker sequences in the reason — neutralise, never drop silently and never rewrite the reason into a paraphrase (task rail 1: the reason reaches the seat verbatim EXCEPT the markers). Assert it: a reason containing `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` and one containing `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` each produce composed text whose sentence contains NEITHER sequence, while the rest of the reason survives character-for-character. Mutate the neutralisation away and confirm the arm reds — an unfenced marker is invisible in a passing test suite.

THE SIX-LINE WIRING. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts:244 `compilerInstructions: (goalId) => { ... }` currently reads the goal catalog brief; it now calls the composer with that brief plus `latestRejectionReason(...)`. The file is 477 lines and ALREADY over the cap, so this row is permitted growth of at most SIX lines (DoD 4) — that is the entire reason the module in step 2 is pure and lives elsewhere. Do not refactor the file, do not 'tidy while here', and do not extract anything: three other rows are serialised behind this same file and a drive-by refactor would collide with all of them. Add the source-text pin DoD 2 requires, modelled on the existing fence pin in agent-wrapper-main.test.ts (:135-166): assert the composer call text appears EXACTLY ONCE, and prove the pin works by deleting the call and confirming it reds — a source-text pin that passes with the code removed is decoration.

THE MISSION ARM (DoD 2's second half). Prove the composed instructions actually reach a compiler seat's mission BETWEEN the operator markers: build the mission through `compilerMission` (agent-mission-text.ts:78) with an instructions string carrying a rejection, and assert the `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason>` sentence appears INSIDE the `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS ... OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` block — not merely somewhere in the text, because outside the block it would read as daemon-authored instruction rather than as the operator's words. State in the step note WHICH file the arm lands in (agent-mission-text.test.ts or the wrapper-main pin) as DoD 2 requires you to name. If it lands in agent-mission-text.test.ts, expect a rebase against task-f79d38b1, which is rewriting that file's compiler sentence.

THE REAL-PROCESS JOURNEY (DoD 3), in the NODE e2e lane — `pnpm test:e2e` runs vitest over tests/e2e. REUSE J4 FIRST: tests/e2e/foundation/j4-replan-harness.ts already exports `readAffordanceSurface` (:73), `stepFor` (:87), `deltaNode` (:94) and `replanCommand` (:110), and j4-replan-handoff.e2e.test.ts already drives a real daemon + real wrapper + fake-agent.mjs seat double. Measure how J4 scripts the double's MCP calls and drives the wrapper, and add a j5 harness ONLY if J4's cannot be parameterised (prefer reuse — say which you did and why). New tests/e2e/foundation/j5-plan-reject-replan.e2e.test.ts: a source-bound goal compiles (the double submits a one-node decomposition) -> the operator REJECTs with a reason over the REAL HTTP wire (approval.decide_intent, decision REJECT) -> the wrapper re-staffs the compiler step -> THE DOUBLE'S MISSION CARRIES `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason>`, asserted from the mission the double ECHOES TO A FILE the test reads (that echo is the only way to see what the seat actually received) -> the double submits a DIFFERENT decomposition under a NEW node key -> the successor is offered for approval -> the operator APPROVEs -> the activation event is read back FROM THE STORE. Every process real except the seat, which goes through the real MCP wire with a scoped bearer and NEVER writes to the store directly (task rail 3).

TEARDOWN, DRILLS, GATES. (a) TEARDOWN PROOF (DoD 3): the journey leaves no surviving process — assert by pid liveness after the test, reusing whatever reaped-pid check the J-series already uses rather than inventing a second one. A leaked daemon or wrapper holds its port and reds the NEXT e2e run, which then looks like an unrelated flake. (b) DRILLS (DoD 4: 'every arm mutated red once'), recorded in a step note: strip the composer call from agent-wrapper-main.ts -> the step-4 source pin reds; remove the marker neutralisation -> the step-3 fence arm reds; make `latestRejectionReason` return the FIRST rejection instead of the latest -> the rejected-twice arm reds. Restore each; the new modules under apps/daemon/src/planning/ and tests/e2e/foundation/ are UNTRACKED until committed, and `git diff` is blind to untracked paths, so prove those restores by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup in %TEMP% suffixed by worker id, in a call SEPARATE from the restore (global rail 13). agent-wrapper-main.ts is tracked, so an empty `git diff` is sound proof there. (c) SIZE PROOF: `wc -l apps/daemon/src/planning/rejection-instructions.ts` <= 120, and agent-wrapper-main.ts growth <= 6 lines against the baseline recorded in step 1 — quote both numbers. (d) GATES with count lines quoted (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e` with the new test listed by name in the output. Named verification command for completion: `pnpm test:e2e`.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, composing the rejection sentence inside agent-wrapper-main.ts: the file is 477 lines and already over the cap, three other rows are serialised behind it, and DoD 4 caps this row's growth at six lines — hence a pure module elsewhere and a one-call wiring. REJECTED, dropping a reason that contains the operator markers: task rail 1 says the reason reaches the seat verbatim EXCEPT the markers, which are neutralised; dropping it silently would hide the operator's actual words and rewriting it would put daemon prose in the operator's mouth. REJECTED, a fresh e2e harness: j4-replan-harness.ts already drives a real daemon, real wrapper and a fake-agent seat double and exports the surface helpers this journey needs; the plan requires reuse unless parameterisation genuinely fails, and requires saying which. REJECTED, asserting the seat's mission from the daemon's side: what matters is what the SEAT received, so the double echoes its mission to a file the test reads — asserting the daemon's output would pass even if the mission never reached the process. REJECTED, letting the seat double write to the store: task rail 3 requires the real MCP wire with a scoped bearer, or the journey proves the fixture rather than the product.

planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — the marker fence. The operator's rejection reason is stored verbatim by child 1 and embedded in a single template line; a reason containing `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` closes the block early and the remainder reads to the seat as daemon-authored mission text. It is invisible in a passing suite, so step 3 asserts both sequences and step 7 mutates the neutralisation away to prove the arm bites. SECOND — the over-cap file. agent-wrapper-main.ts is 477 lines with three rows serialised behind it; a drive-by refactor here collides with all of them, and the six-line budget is meaningless without the baseline step 1 records. THIRD — a source-text pin that passes with the code removed is decoration; step 4 requires proving it reds. FOURTH — 'latest rejection' vs 'first rejection' is the kind of fold bug a single-rejection test never sees; the rejected-twice arm and its drill exist for that. FIFTH — asserting the mission from the daemon's side would pass even if it never reached the seat; the double must echo what it actually received. SIXTH — drill restores on UNTRACKED new files need an out-of-tree SHA256 comparison, because `git diff` is blind to them (global rail 13). SEVENTH — a leaked daemon or wrapper from the journey reds the NEXT e2e run and reads as an unrelated flake.
